title: Contract Thermostat: Drift Detection & Repair Playbook for Structured Outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Implement a 'thermostat' for structured-output contracts that continuously monitors schema adherence and automatically tunes constrained-decoding strictness or triggers controlled fallbacks. Motivation: we frequently see gradual drift in real traffic (prompt distribution, model weight updates, or interleaved toolcalls) that increases schema-violation surface area. Existing static thresholds cause either noisy alerts or silent regressions. The thermostat will provide an operational feedback loop: detect drift, surface diagnostics, run repair strategies (tighten/loosen decoder constraints, switch to compatibility shim, or route to fallback model), and record an auditable trail for postmortem and ML evals. Scope: 1) Instrument schema-compat telemetry across streaming and tool-calling flows (schema_match_rate, partial_emit_rate, sentinel_rewrites, decode_retries, latency_p95). 2) Implement a controller service (thermostat) that computes short/long windows and exposes a decision API. 3) Wire thermostat decisions into runtime: constrained-decoder parameter adjustments, canary routing, and automatic graceful fallback to compatibility layer. 4) Build a synthetic drift harness and canary rollout plan, plus runbook for manual overrides and escalation. Out of scope: model retraining pipelines and customer-visible UI beyond alert links and dashboard snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat emits a rolling schema_adherence score (1m and 1h windows) for each route and model variant
When injected schema drift >= 20% on canary traffic, thermostat triggers configured action within 5 minutes
False-positive alert rate < 2% during 72-hour baseline on control traffic
End-to-end latency p95 impact on canary <= +20ms when thermostat adjusts decoder parameters
Automated fallback path (compatibility shim) maintains functional responses for 95% of previously failing prompts
Playbook exists with manual override, observable signals, and postmortem checklist
test_plan: Unit tests for thermostat decision logic with synthetic metric series (gradual drift, sudden jump, oscillation)
Integration tests: thermostat API toggles constrained-decoder params and runtime honors adjustments in single-node dev environment
Chaos suite: interrupt streaming responses midway and ensure partial_emit_rate signals are correctly attributed and cause no runaway actions
Canary scenario: route 2% traffic to canary model with progressive drift injection (0 -> 40% schema corruption over 30 minutes) and verify detection and fallback
Cross-model regression: run compatibility shim against historical eval suite and compare semantic fidelity metrics before/after fallback
Load test: ensure thermostat decision latency < 200ms at 1k/sec metric ingestion; no more than 5% CPU overhead on metric workers
steps: Design: finalize thermostat thresholds, windows, and action matrix with PM and Applied ML
Instrumentation: add schema_adherence, partial_emit_rate, and sentinel_rewrite counters to runtime and SDK layers
Controller: implement thermostat service with sliding-window aggregators and decision API
Runtime integration: accept decision API and expose constrained-decoder toggles and routing flags
Test harness: build synthetic drift injector for streaming + toolcall interleaves
Dashboards & alerts: create per-route dashboards and PagerDuty/Slack alerting with runbook links
Canary rollout: deploy to staging, then production canary, exercise injections, and validate acceptance criteria
Docs & runbook: publish operational playbook and postmortem template in Confluence
